title: AI Infrastructure and Hardware
answer: GPUs, NPUs, TPUs, chip fabs, memory and storage, plus the datacenters, power, cooling, and networking underneath them.

reading.body:
AI infrastructure is organized into six layers, from the GPU itself down to the networking fabric that links racks into a cluster, and the memory supply chain is treated as its own subject.

The structure follows the physical stack rather than a market map. Silicon comes first: GPUs, then purpose-built accelerators outside the GPU line, then the fabs that manufacture the chips. Memory and storage sit next to the accelerator, and networking covers both the scale-up fabric inside a rack and the scale-out fabric between racks. The counts are small, six entries for GPUs and five each for fabrication and networking, so this is a taxonomy with sparse coverage rather than a census.

The inclusion of memory supply as a distinct section is the notable editorial choice. It is framed around who makes the memory on an accelerator, the absence of any index tracking its price, the effect on PC memory prices, and how HBM4 changes the chip. That framing connects the accelerator to the wider supply chain and to prices outside AI, which is where memory stops being a component and becomes a constraint.

What the data does not contain is any of the substance behind these headings. There are no companies, no process nodes, no throughput figures, no power or cooling entries despite the summary naming datacenters, power, and cooling. The page establishes the shape of the stack and nothing about its capacity, cost, or geography.

items.claim: Groq and NVIDIA entered a non-exclusive licensing agreement for Groq's inference technology, with Groq's founder and other leaders joining NVIDIA while Groq stayed independent.

AMD and OpenAI agreed a partnership for up to 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct accelerators, the first gigawatt from the second half of 2026, with OpenAI receiving a warrant for AMD shares tied to milestones.
HPE and NVIDIA announced NVIDIA AI Computing by HPE, a jointly built private AI stack combining NVIDIA GPUs and AI Enterprise software with HPE GreenLake.
